topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It welcomes students, introduces the lecture series structure, and outlines the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer originates through accumulated genetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the classification of benign versus malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They characterize the histopathological features, metastatic pathways, progression risks, and nomenclature distinguishing benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the local and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair physiological functions to cause disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative incidence of cancer in humans and animals
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the epidemiological frequency and mortality rates of different cancers in humans and compare them with tumor patterns across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the rationale for early detection and evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of screening programs across major cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and logistical details for upcoming sessions.
